title: [Electroacupuncture at Dong's Sanqixue combined with auricular point sticking in treatment of post-operative complications of complex anal fistula: a real world research].
evidence_supporting_decision: The abstract explicitly states that 318 surgical patients were analyzed retrospectively and groups were formed according to whether combined EA plus auricular point sticking had been accepted; nearest-neighbor matching was then used.
concise_rationale: Retrospective matched real-world comparison, not a randomized controlled trial.
intervention: EA at Dong Sanqixue combined with auricular point sticking
comparator: No combined treatment; retrospectively matched control
timing_description: Postoperative treatment; exact first-treatment time not reported.
notes: DOI 10.13703/j.0255-2930.20200711-k0003; Ref ID 34259403. Primary exclusion is explicit retrospective allocation; intervention is also inseparable from auricular point sticking.

title: Evaluation of electroacupuncture for symptom modification in a rodent model of spontaneous osteoarthritis.
evidence_supporting_decision: The title identifies a rodent model and the abstract reports ten 12-month-old male Hartley guinea pigs, euthanasia, joint histology, and gene expression.
concise_rationale: Animal electroacupuncture experiment in guinea pigs, not an adult human perioperative trial.
timing_description: not_applicable

title: Prospective, Single-Center Comparison of Transcranial Direct Current Stimulation Plus Electroacupuncture and Standard Analgesia in Patients After Total Knee Arthroplasty: Effect on Rehabilitation and Functional Recovery.
evidence_supporting_decision: The experimental group received both transcranial direct current stimulation and electroacupuncture in addition to multimodal analgesia, while the control group received multimodal analgesia alone.
concise_rationale: EA is embedded in an inseparable tDCS-plus-EA intervention bundle, so its independent effect cannot be extracted.
intervention: Transcranial direct current stimulation plus electroacupuncture
timing_description: Postoperative analgesia method; exact EA initiation time not reported.
notes: DOI 10.12659/MSM.930363; Ref ID 34103464. Allocation was also described as division according to postoperative analgesia method rather than randomization.

title: [Effect of electroacupuncture at Neiguan (PC 6) on pulmonary function during one-lung ventilation in patients with lobectomy].
evidence_supporting_decision: Sixty lobectomy patients were randomly allocated; all received general anaesthesia and one-lung ventilation, while the intervention group received needle EA at PC6 from 30 minutes before induction through surgery. Clinical outcomes included complications, PCA use, and hospital stay.
concise_rationale: Clear randomized perioperative needle-EA trial under general anaesthesia with separable usual-care comparison and eligible clinical outcomes.
comparator: Identical general anaesthesia and surgery without EA
timing_description: EA began 30 minutes before anaesthesia induction and continued until the end of surgery.

title: [Electroacupuncture combined with acupoint catgut embedding for postoperative pain after fistulotomy].
evidence_supporting_decision: The randomized arms were EA alone, acupoint catgut embedding alone, and their combination; there was no sham EA, usual-care, no-stimulation, attention-control, or other balanced eligible comparator.
concise_rationale: The only separable EA comparison is against another active acupuncture-related intervention, with no eligible control arm.
intervention: Needle electroacupuncture alone or combined with acupoint catgut embedding
comparator: Acupoint catgut embedding or combination therapy
timing_description: All interventions were performed 30 minutes before fistulotomy.

title: Opposing and Operated Side Electroacupuncture Generates Similar Analgesic Effects on Pain after Knee Surgery.
evidence_supporting_decision: The abstract explicitly describes knee surgery and electroacupuncture experiments in Sprague Dawley rats.
concise_rationale: Animal postoperative electroacupuncture experiment, not an adult human trial.
timing_description: not_applicable

title: Effects of Transcutaneous Electrical Acupoint Stimulation on Postoperative Cognitive Decline in Elderly Patients: A Pilot Study.
evidence_supporting_decision: The randomized TEAS trial involved elderly patients undergoing laparoscopic radical colon cancer surgery and stimulation from 30 minutes before anaesthesia induction through surgery, but the abstract does not explicitly identify the anaesthetic technique as general anaesthesia.
concise_rationale: Otherwise eligible perioperative TEAS RCT; general anaesthesia remains the single realistic full-text uncertainty.
intervention: TEAS at bilateral Hegu, Neiguan, and Zusanli
timing_description: From 30 minutes before anaesthesia induction until the end of surgery.
notes: DOI 10.2147/CIA.S309082; Ref ID 33976542. Laparoscopic surgery alone was not treated as proof of general anaesthesia.

title: Smartphone-controlled patch electro-acupuncture versus conventional pain relief during colonoscopy: a randomized controlled trial.
evidence_supporting_decision: The randomized patch electro-acupuncture intervention was used during colonoscopy, with rescue sedation as needed; no operative surgery was performed.
concise_rationale: Colonoscopy is a non-operative endoscopic procedure and does not meet the operative-surgery population criterion.
timing_description: During colonoscopy.

title: Perioperative Electroacupuncture Can Accelerate the Recovery of Gastrointestinal Function in Cancer Patients Undergoing Pancreatectomy or Gastrectomy: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
evidence_supporting_decision: This is a randomized sham-controlled transcutaneous acupoint-stimulation trial in pancreatectomy or gastrectomy patients, but the abstract states only that stimulation was given once daily in the afternoon and does not identify when the first session began relative to surgery.
concise_rationale: Otherwise eligible perioperative TEAS trial; exact first-session timing must be verified at full text.
intervention: Transcutaneous electrical stimulation at GV20, PC6, ST25, and ST36
timing_description: Once daily in the afternoon; first session relative to surgery not stated.
notes: DOI 10.1155/2021/5594263; Ref ID 33859707; NCT03291574. Major pancreatectomy/gastrectomy procedures make general anaesthesia highly evident.

title: [Electroacupuncture in the prevention and treatment of sore throat and nausea and vomiting after gastrointestinal surgery: a randomized controlled trial].
evidence_supporting_decision: The intervention group received manual acupuncture at LU11 before general anaesthesia plus EA at LU5 and LI4 through surgery, while the control group did not receive these components.
concise_rationale: EA is combined with an additional manual-acupuncture component that is absent from the control and cannot be separated.
intervention: Manual acupuncture at LU11 plus needle EA at LU5 and LI4
timing_description: Manual acupuncture began 30 minutes before general anaesthesia; EA continued until surgery ended.

title: Efficacy of Electroacupuncture Combined with Tropisetron in Treating Carboprost Tromethamine-Induced Nausea and Vomiting during Cesarean Section under Lumbar Anesthesia.
evidence_supporting_decision: The title and abstract explicitly state that the cesarean sections were performed under lumbar anaesthesia.
concise_rationale: Operative population used neuraxial/lumbar anaesthesia without general anaesthesia.
intervention: Needle electroacupuncture alone or with tropisetron
timing_description: During cesarean section.

title: Short-term effect of electroacupuncture on rehabilitation after arthroscopic triangular fibrocartilage complex repair: a randomised study.
evidence_supporting_decision: The randomized trial added EA to identical active rehabilitation after arthroscopic TFCC repair, but reports only a 4-week treatment course without stating when the first EA session began; the anaesthetic technique is also unreported.
concise_rationale: Eligibility remains possible if surgery used general anaesthesia and EA began within 24 postoperative hours, but both require full-text verification.
intervention: Needle electroacupuncture plus standard active rehabilitation
comparator: Identical standard active rehabilitation without EA
timing_description: Four-week postoperative rehabilitation course; first EA session not stated.
notes: DOI 10.1186/s13018-021-02361-1; Ref ID 33761976. General anaesthesia is also unclear.

title: The effectiveness of electro-acupuncture combined with dyclonine hydrochloride in relieving the side effects of gastroscopy: a controlled trial.
evidence_supporting_decision: The study assessed EA and local anaesthetic during diagnostic gastroscopy rather than operative surgery.
concise_rationale: Gastroscopy is a non-operative endoscopic procedure and is outside the surgical population.
intervention: Electroacupuncture alone or combined with oral dyclonine
comparator: Dyclonine alone or active combination arms
timing_description: During gastroscopy.

title: Transcutaneous Electrical Acupoint Stimulation Combined with Dexamethasone and Tropisetron Prevents Postoperative Nausea and Vomiting in Female Patients Undergoing Laparoscopic Sleeve Gastrectomy: a Prospective, Randomized Controlled Trial.
evidence_supporting_decision: The randomized comparison balanced dexamethasone and tropisetron across groups and added TEAS only, but the abstract does not report when TEAS was first delivered relative to surgery.
concise_rationale: Potentially eligible TEAS RCT with balanced antiemetics; first-session timing requires full-text verification.
comparator: Identical dexamethasone and tropisetron without TEAS
timing_description: TEAS timing not stated in the abstract.
notes: DOI 10.1007/s11695-020-05205-9; Ref ID 33650089. Sleeve gastrectomy makes general anaesthesia highly evident, but full text can confirm.

title: The Effect of Transcutaneous Electrical Acupoint Stimulation on Postoperative Catheter-Related Bladder Discomfort in Patients Undergoing Transurethral Resection of the Prostate.
evidence_supporting_decision: Prospective randomized double-blind controlled trial in TURP under general anaesthesia; TEAS was delivered for 30 minutes before anaesthesia at explicitly named acupoints and clinical recovery outcomes were reported.
concise_rationale: Clear preoperative TEAS RCT under general anaesthesia with separable control and eligible postoperative outcomes.
intervention: TEAS at RN3-RN7 and bilateral BL32-BL34
timing_description: TEAS for 30 minutes before general anaesthesia.

title: Effects of Transcutaneous Electrical Acupoint Stimulation (TEAS) on Postoperative Recovery in Patients with Gastric Cancer: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
evidence_supporting_decision: The randomized gastrectomy trial delivered TEAS on postoperative days 1-3, but the abstract does not establish the elapsed time from surgery to the first POD1 session.
concise_rationale: Potentially eligible postoperative TEAS RCT; POD1 wording alone does not prove initiation within 24 hours.
timing_description: TEAS on POD1-POD3; exact elapsed start time not reported.
notes: DOI 10.2147/CMAR.S292325; Ref ID 33603487. Gastrectomy makes general anaesthesia highly evident.

title: [Comparative study between electroacupuncture at Neima point and Neiguan (PC 6) and epidural nerve block for preemptive analgesia in patients undergoing thoracic surgery].
evidence_supporting_decision: Randomized three-arm radical esophagectomy trial under general anaesthesia includes an independently extractable EA arm receiving 30 minutes of preinduction EA and a general-anaesthesia-only control arm; all groups received PCIA.
concise_rationale: Clear separable EA-versus-usual-care comparison in randomized surgery under general anaesthesia.
intervention: Needle EA at bilateral Neima and PC6
comparator: General anaesthesia alone; separate epidural-block arm also present
timing_description: EA for 30 minutes before anaesthesia induction.

title: Perioperative transcutaneous electrical acupoint stimulation for improving postoperative gastrointestinal function: A randomized controlled trial.
evidence_supporting_decision: Stratified randomized sham-controlled trial in major gastric or colorectal surgery; TEAS at LI4, PC6, ST36, and ST37 began 30 minutes before anaesthesia and continued through surgery, with eligible postoperative gastrointestinal and recovery outcomes.
concise_rationale: Clear perioperative TEAS-versus-sham RCT in major abdominal surgery with eligible timing and outcomes.
intervention: TEAS at LI4, PC6, ST36, and ST37
timing_description: From 30 minutes before anaesthesia until surgery end, repeated POD1-POD3.
notes: DOI 10.1016/j.joim.2021.01.005; Ref ID 33495134; ChiCTR1900023263. Major gastric/colorectal surgery makes general anaesthesia highly evident.

title: Effects of transcutaneous electrical acupoint stimulation on perioperative immune function and postoperative analgesia in patients undergoing radical mastectomy: A randomized controlled trial.
evidence_supporting_decision: Randomized sham-controlled radical-mastectomy trial; TEAS at LI4, PC6, and ST36 was delivered before anaesthesia induction and again 4 and 12 hours postoperatively, with pain, opioid use, PONV, and adverse-event outcomes.
concise_rationale: Clear perioperative TEAS-versus-sham RCT with eligible timing and postoperative clinical outcomes.
intervention: TEAS at bilateral LI4, PC6, and ST36
timing_description: Thirty minutes before anaesthesia induction and at 4 and 12 postoperative hours.
notes: DOI 10.3892/etm.2021.9615; Ref ID 33488793; ChiCTR1800017768. Radical mastectomy with anaesthesia induction makes general anaesthesia highly evident.

title: The acupoint herbal plaster for the prevention and treatment of postoperative nausea and vomiting after PLIF with general anesthesia: study protocol for a multicenter randomized controlled trial.
evidence_supporting_decision: The title identifies a study protocol and the abstract uses future tense, stating that the trial will be conducted and reporting no participant results.
timing_description: not_applicable
notes: DOI 10.1186/s13063-021-05037-7; Ref ID 33482878; ChiCTR1800015768. Planned intervention is also an ineligible herbal acupoint plaster.

title: [Effect of transcutaneous electrical acupoint stimulation on venous thrombosis after lung cancer surgery: a randomized controlled trial].
evidence_supporting_decision: The randomized three-arm lung-cancer surgery trial contains a separable TEAS-plus-rehabilitation versus identical-rehabilitation comparison, but the abstract states only twice-daily treatment for 5 days and does not identify the first session time after surgery.
concise_rationale: Potentially eligible postoperative TEAS comparison; initiation within 24 hours requires full-text confirmation.
intervention: TEAS at ST36, SP10, SP6 and other points plus early functional exercise
comparator: Identical early functional exercise without TEAS
timing_description: Twice daily for 5 postoperative days; first session time not stated.
notes: DOI 10.13703/j.0255-2930.20191204-k0007; Ref ID 33415872. Radical lung resection makes general anaesthesia highly evident.

title: Transcutaneous Electrical Acupoint Stimulation Reduces Postoperative Analgesic Requirement in Patients Undergoing Inguinal Hernia Repair: A Randomized, Placebo-Controlled Study.
evidence_supporting_decision: The prospective randomized TEAS-versus-sham and PCA-only trial reports a standardized anaesthetic technique but does not identify it as general anaesthesia; TEAS timing is also not stated in the abstract.
concise_rationale: Strongly relevant TEAS RCT, but anaesthetic technique and first-session timing require full-text confirmation.
comparator: Sham TEAS plus PCA or PCA only
timing_description: TEAS timing not reported in the abstract.
notes: DOI 10.3390/jcm10010146; Ref ID 33406735. Known sentinel candidate; retained for full-text verification.

title: A randomized pilot study of electro-acupuncture treatment for hysterosalpingography pain relief and related anxiety.
evidence_supporting_decision: The intervention was delivered before hysterosalpingography, a diagnostic imaging procedure rather than operative surgery.
concise_rationale: Non-operative hysterosalpingography population, outside the review scope.
timing_description: Twenty minutes before hysterosalpingography.

title: Multicentre randomised controlled clinical trial of electroacupuncture with usual care for patients with non-acute pain after back surgery.
evidence_supporting_decision: The study enrolled patients with non-acute low back pain after back surgery and delivered EA twice weekly for 4 weeks as conservative treatment, rather than initiating treatment in the acute perioperative window.
concise_rationale: Treatment targeted non-acute postoperative pain during later conservative care, outside the ≤24-hour initiation window.
timing_description: Twice weekly for 4 weeks in patients with non-acute pain after surgery.

title: [Transcutaneous electrical acupoint stimulation relieves post-operative nausea and vomiting possibly by reducing serum motilin secretion in patients undergoing laparoscopic surgery].
evidence_supporting_decision: Randomized four-arm laparoscopic-surgery trial under general anaesthesia compared three separable TEAS acupoint combinations with a general-anaesthesia control. TEAS began 30 minutes before induction and continued through surgery; PONV was reported.
concise_rationale: Clear perioperative TEAS randomized trial under general anaesthesia with usual-care control and eligible clinical outcome.
intervention: TEAS at combinations of PC6, LI4, ST36, and SP6
timing_description: From 30 minutes before anaesthesia induction until the end of surgery.

title: Effects of transcutaneous electrical acupuncture point stimulation on peripheral capillary oxygen saturation in elderly patients undergoing colonoscopy with sedation: a prospective randomized controlled trial.
evidence_supporting_decision: Randomized TEAS-versus-sham study during colonoscopy under sedation.
concise_rationale: Non-operative colonoscopy under sedation, not surgery under general anaesthesia.
timing_description: Twenty minutes during colonoscopy preparation.

title: The Preventive Effect of Computed Tomography Image-Guided Electroacupuncture Combined with Continuous Femoral Nerve Block on Deep Vein Thrombosis After Total Knee Arthroplasty Based on an Adaptive Algorithm.
evidence_supporting_decision: The randomized study had four groups but the abstract does not describe their arm structure; EA is discussed with continuous femoral nerve block, so an independently extractable EA comparison may or may not exist.
concise_rationale: Four-arm trial may contain a separable EA contrast, but intervention balance and anaesthetic technique require full-text review.
intervention: Image-guided EA with continuous femoral nerve block
timing_description: Postoperative context; exact first EA time not stated.

title: Postoperative analgesic efficacy of ear acupuncture in patients undergoing abdominal hysterectomy: a randomized controlled trial.
evidence_supporting_decision: Electrical stimulation was delivered through needles at four auricular points, followed by permanent ear press needles.
concise_rationale: Auricular electroacupuncture/ear acupuncture is explicitly excluded.
intervention: Electric ear acupuncture followed by press needles
timing_description: Perioperative and 24 hours postoperative.
notes: DOI 10.1186/s12871-020-01187-4; Ref ID 33167893; PACTR201903770607799. Spinal-only anaesthesia is also ineligible.

title: Effects of Transcutaneous Electrical Acupoint Stimulation on the Postoperative Sleep Quality and Pain of Patients After Video-Assisted Thoracoscopic Surgery: A Prospective, Randomized Controlled Trial.
evidence_supporting_decision: Randomized video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery trial; TEAS was delivered the night before surgery, at surgery end, and on subsequent nights, with postoperative sleep, pain, PONV, and dizziness outcomes.
concise_rationale: Clear perioperative TEAS randomized trial with eligible preoperative timing and clinical recovery outcomes.
timing_description: First session the night before surgery; another at surgery end.
notes: DOI 10.2147/NSS.S270739; Ref ID 33154688. Video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery makes general anaesthesia highly evident.

title: Decreased Synovial Fluid Biomarkers Levels Are Associated with Rehabilitation of Function and Pain in Rotator Cuff Tear Patients Following Electroacupuncture Therapy.
evidence_supporting_decision: Patients with rotator cuff tears received EA as conservative therapy with 6-week and 6-month follow-up; no operative surgery was described.
concise_rationale: Non-operative conservative treatment of rotator cuff tear.
timing_description: Conservative treatment, not perioperative.

title: [Effect of transcutaneous electrical acupoint stimulation on catheter related bladder discomfort after ureteroscopic lithotripsy].
evidence_supporting_decision: Randomized sham-controlled ureteroscopic lithotripsy under general anaesthesia; TEAS at CV4, CV3, ST36, and SP6 was delivered for 30 minutes before induction, with postoperative bladder discomfort, pain, anaesthetic use, and adverse events.
concise_rationale: Clear preoperative TEAS-versus-sham RCT under general anaesthesia with eligible outcomes.
intervention: TEAS at CV4, CV3, ST36, and SP6
timing_description: Thirty minutes before anaesthesia induction.

title: Pretreatment with transcutaneous electrical acupoint stimulation to prevent postoperative ileus in patients undergoing laparoscopic colon surgery: study protocol for a randomised controlled trial.
evidence_supporting_decision: The title identifies a study protocol; the abstract states the trial will be conducted and was recruiting, with no participant results.
timing_description: not_applicable

title: Effectiveness and safety of polydioxanone thread-embedding acupuncture (TEA) and electroacupuncture (EA) treatment for knee osteoarthritis (KOA) patients with postoperative pain: An assessor-blinded, randomized, controlled pilot trial.
evidence_supporting_decision: The methods/design abstract uses future tense and describes a planned 36-patient randomized pilot trial without participant results.
timing_description: not_applicable
notes: DOI 10.1097/MD.0000000000021184; Ref ID 32791693; KCT0004804. Planned intervention also combines thread-embedding acupuncture with EA and targets persistent later postoperative pain.

title: Using electroacupuncture to recover muscle strength in patients with knee osteoarthritis after total knee arthroplasty: a study protocol for a double-blinded, randomized, and placebo-controlled trial.
evidence_supporting_decision: The title identifies a study protocol and the abstract states that participants will be randomized and outcomes will be measured, without results.
timing_description: not_applicable

title: Electroacupuncture Improves Cognition in Rats With Sepsis-Associated Encephalopathy.
evidence_supporting_decision: The study used rats randomized around cecal ligation and puncture and assessed water-maze cognition, brain histology, and oxidative stress.
timing_description: not_applicable

title: GABAergic Inhibition of Spinal Cord Dorsal Horns Contributes to Analgesic Effect of Electroacupuncture in Incisional Neck Pain Rats.
evidence_supporting_decision: The study created an incisional neck pain model in male rats and evaluated EA effects on pain thresholds and spinal GABA pathways.
concise_rationale: Animal mechanistic electroacupuncture experiment in rats.
timing_description: not_applicable

title: Impact of Electroacupuncture Stimulation on Postoperative Constipation for Patients Undergoing Brain Tumor Surgery.
evidence_supporting_decision: Randomized brain-tumor resection trial included a separable EA arm and no-treatment control with postoperative constipation outcomes, but the abstract does not report when EA first began after surgery.
concise_rationale: Potentially eligible postoperative EA RCT; first-session timing needs full-text verification.
timing_description: Postoperative treatment; initiation time unreported.
notes: DOI 10.1097/JNN.0000000000000531; Ref ID 32675583. Brain tumor resection makes general anaesthesia highly evident.

title: Transcutaneous electrical acupuncture stimulation (TEAS) for gastrointestinal dysfunction in adults undergoing abdominal surgery: study protocol for a prospective randomized controlled trial.
evidence_supporting_decision: The title identifies a study protocol and the abstract states the trial will be performed, with planned outcomes and no participant results.
timing_description: not_applicable
notes: DOI 10.1186/s13063-020-04470-4; Ref ID 32631387; ChiCTR1900023263. Protocol companion to results report at Covidence #437.

title: Effect of Transcutaneous Electrical Acupoint Stimulation on One-Lung Ventilation-Induced Lung Injury in Patients Undergoing Esophageal Cancer Operation.
evidence_supporting_decision: Randomized sham-controlled esophageal cancer surgery trial with one-lung ventilation; TEAS at BL13, LI4, and ST36 was delivered for 30 minutes before anaesthesia induction, and postoperative pulmonary complications, drainage duration, and length of stay were reported.
concise_rationale: Clear preoperative TEAS-versus-sham randomized major surgery trial with eligible outcomes.
intervention: TEAS at BL13, LI4, and ST36
timing_description: Thirty minutes before anaesthesia induction.
notes: DOI 10.1155/2020/9018701; Ref ID 32595749. One-lung ventilation establishes general anaesthesia.

title: A Malaysian retrospective study of acupuncture-assisted anesthesia in breast lump excision.
evidence_supporting_decision: The title and methods explicitly identify a retrospective medical-record review of 17 breast lump excisions.
concise_rationale: Retrospective uncontrolled case series, not an RCT.
timing_description: During breast lump excision.
notes: DOI 10.1177/0964528420920307; Ref ID 32539426. Procedure used local anaesthetic rather than general anaesthesia.

title: Histopathological evaluation of the role of negative electrical charge on renal ischemia/reperfusion injuries on brain and heart tissues in rat.
evidence_supporting_decision: The experiment randomized 24 Sprague Dawley rats and assessed heart and brain histopathology after renal ischemia/reperfusion.
timing_description: not_applicable

title: Effect of Electroacupuncture on Postoperative Gastrointestinal Recovery in Patients Undergoing Thoracoscopic Surgery: A Feasibility Study.
evidence_supporting_decision: Randomized VATS segmentectomy/lobectomy feasibility trial compared EA plus usual care with usual care alone. EA at PC6, ST36, and ST37 was delivered 24 hours preoperatively and 4 and 24 hours postoperatively, with GI recovery, PONV, pain, and stay outcomes.
concise_rationale: Clear perioperative needle-EA randomized surgical trial with separable usual-care comparison and eligible timing.
intervention: Needle EA at PC6, ST36, and ST37
timing_description: 24 hours before surgery and 4 and 24 hours after surgery.
notes: DOI 10.12659/MSM.920648; Ref ID 32445558. VATS lung resection makes general anaesthesia highly evident; paravertebral block appears common background care.

title: [Effect of early electroacupuncture intervention on conscious state of patients after traumatic brain injury surgery].
evidence_supporting_decision: Randomized TBI-surgery trial added daily EA at PC6 and GV26 to identical drug treatment, but describes intervention only as early postoperative treatment without stating elapsed time to the first session.
concise_rationale: Potentially eligible postoperative EA RCT; first treatment within 24 hours requires full-text confirmation.
intervention: Needle EA at PC6 and GV26 plus standard drugs
comparator: Identical awakening and neurotrophic drugs without EA
timing_description: Described as early intervention once daily for 14 days; first session time not stated.
notes: DOI 10.13703/j.0255-2930.20190506-0005; Ref ID 32394653. Traumatic brain injury surgery makes general anaesthesia highly evident.

title: Opposing needling for analgesia and rehabilitation after unilateral total knee arthroplasty: a randomized, sham-controlled trial protocol.
evidence_supporting_decision: The title and methods explicitly identify a randomized sham-controlled trial protocol; all interventions and outcomes are described in future tense without results.
timing_description: not_applicable

title: Transcutaneous Electrical Acustimulation Improves Gastrointestinal Disturbances Induced by Transcatheter Arterial Chemoembolization in Patients With Liver Cancers.
evidence_supporting_decision: The randomized TEA trial involved transcatheter arterial chemoembolization for liver cancer, a percutaneous interventional procedure rather than operative surgery.
concise_rationale: TACE is a non-operative percutaneous intervention outside the surgical population.
intervention: Transcutaneous electrical acustimulation at ST36 and PC6
timing_description: From procedure day 0 through day 2.

title: [Effect and safety of electroacupuncture analgesia at the latent stage of labor on the epidural analgesia].
evidence_supporting_decision: Participants were primiparous women undergoing vaginal delivery with epidural analgesia, not operative surgery.
concise_rationale: Labor and vaginal delivery are non-operative and used epidural rather than general anaesthesia.
intervention: Electrical acupoint stimulation at LI4 and SP6
timing_description: During latent labor.

title: [Effect of transcutaneous electrical acupoint stimulation on postoperative olfactory memory disorder and plasma melatonin in patients with general anesthesia of sevoflurane].
evidence_supporting_decision: Randomized gynecological/urological operative study under sevoflurane general anaesthesia; TEAS at LI20 and GV29 began 10 minutes before induction and continued through surgery, with postoperative olfactory-memory recovery assessed.
concise_rationale: Clear perioperative TEAS randomized trial under general anaesthesia with an eligible postoperative cognitive/sensory recovery outcome.
timing_description: Ten minutes before anaesthesia induction until surgery end.

title: [Effect of electroacupuncture on diaphragmatic function in patients with post-stroke tracheotomy].
evidence_supporting_decision: Participants were post-stroke patients with tracheotomy tubes receiving four weeks of rehabilitation; no operative perioperative population was studied.
intervention: EA added to manual acupuncture and rehabilitation
timing_description: Four-week rehabilitation course.

title: Combined effect of laser acupuncture and electroacupuncture in knee osteoarthritis patients: A protocol for a randomized controlled trial.
evidence_supporting_decision: The title and abstract identify a protocol and describe planned treatment and outcomes in future tense without results.
timing_description: not_applicable
notes: DOI 10.1097/MD.0000000000019541; Ref ID 32195960. Non-operative knee osteoarthritis and laser-acupuncture focus are also outside scope.

title: Effect of electrically stimulating acupoint, Zusanli (ST 36), on patient's recovery after laparoscopic colorectal cancer resection: a randomized controlled trial.
evidence_supporting_decision: Randomized laparoscopic colorectal-resection trial; both groups received the same ERAS anaesthesia management and PCIA, while TEAS at bilateral ST36 was delivered from 30 minutes before anaesthesia through surgery. Clinical pain and GI recovery outcomes were reported.
concise_rationale: Clear perioperative TEAS randomized trial with identical ERAS background care and eligible clinical outcomes.
intervention: TEAS at bilateral ST36 plus identical ERAS care
timing_description: From 30 minutes before anaesthesia until surgery end.
notes: Ref ID 32186016. Laparoscopic colorectal resection with remifentanil-based anaesthesia makes general anaesthesia highly evident.

title: Electroacupuncture promotes peripheral nerve regeneration after facial nerve crush injury and upregulates the expression of glial cell-derived neurotrophic factor.
evidence_supporting_decision: The study randomized New Zealand rabbits with facial nerve crush injury and assessed nerve histology and gene/protein expression.
timing_description: not_applicable

title: Effect of transcutaneous electrical acupoint stimulation on the EC50 of remifentanil suppressing responses to tracheal extubation in elderly patients.
evidence_supporting_decision: Randomized elderly spine-surgery trial with intubation/extubation compared TEAS with control and measured remifentanil dose requirements, but the abstract does not state the TEAS treatment timing or acupoints.
concise_rationale: Potentially eligible perioperative TEAS RCT under general anaesthesia; stimulation timing and acupoint details require full-text verification.
intervention: TEAS; acupoints not stated in abstract
timing_description: Not reported in the abstract.
notes: DOI 10.1097/MD.0000000000013814; Ref ID 30593173. Tracheal extubation establishes general anaesthesia.

title: [Electroacupuncture Treatment Conduced Before and After Surgery Is Better in Promoting Reco-very of Gastrointestinal Function in Colorectal Cancer Patients Undergoing Radical Resection].
evidence_supporting_decision: Randomized four-arm colorectal laparotomy trial under intravenous general anaesthesia compared three separable EA schedules with anaesthesia-only control. EA was delivered one day and/or 30 minutes preoperatively, with one arm also treated one day after surgery.
concise_rationale: Clear perioperative needle-EA randomized surgical trial with usual-care control, eligible timing, and GI recovery outcomes.
intervention: Needle EA at CV12, ST25, PC6, ST36, ST37, and ST39 using different schedules
timing_description: One day before surgery and/or 30 minutes before surgery; one arm also POD1.

title: [Clinical Trial of Electroacupuncture Treatment for Relieving Stress Responses in Patients Undergoing Gastrointestinal Surgery].
evidence_supporting_decision: Randomized gastrointestinal-surgery trial compared postoperative EA plus identical conventional care with conventional care alone. Two EA sessions were given 6 hours apart after surgery, but the first session time is not stated.
concise_rationale: Potentially eligible postoperative EA RCT; initiation within 24 hours requires full-text confirmation.
intervention: Needle EA at bilateral ST36 and PC6 plus conventional care
timing_description: Two postoperative sessions 6 hours apart; first-session time unreported.
notes: DOI 10.13702/j.1000-0607.170617; Ref ID 30585458. Major gastrointestinal surgery makes general anaesthesia highly evident.

title: [Effect of Electroacupuncture of "Weizhong" (BL 40) and "Huantiao" (GB 30) on cAMP-PKA-CREB Signaling of Spinal Cord in Rats with Neuropathic Pain].
evidence_supporting_decision: The study randomized 100 male rats with spared-nerve injury and assessed spinal signaling proteins after EA.
timing_description: not_applicable

title: Transcutaneous Electrical Acupoint Stimulation Accelerates the Recovery of Gastrointestinal Function after Cesarean Section: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
evidence_supporting_decision: Randomized TEAS-versus-sham/no-stimulation cesarean trial reported eligible recovery outcomes, but the abstract does not identify the anaesthetic technique or TEAS timing.
concise_rationale: Eligibility remains possible, but general anaesthesia and first-session timing both require full-text verification.
comparator: Non-acupoint sham stimulation or no stimulation
timing_description: Not reported in the abstract.

title: Acupuncture and related interventions for the treatment of symptoms associated with carpal tunnel syndrome.
evidence_supporting_decision: The abstract reports Cochrane search methods, selection criteria, synthesis of 12 studies, and review conclusions.
concise_rationale: Systematic review, not a primary randomized trial report.
timing_description: not_applicable

title: [Effect of electro-acupuncture at Zusanli acupoint on postoperative T cell immune function in rats].
